activities.anchor: The craft is keeping all three parts turning
activities.caption: file each element — skeleton, body or pulse
activities.name: dramaElementsSort

config.prompt: The machine has three moving parts — file each element:
buckets: characterisation, dialogue, physicality — who and how
pacing, contrast, tension — how it is experienced

items.label: loud against quiet, fast against frozen

config.why: A scene can fail at any level: a perfect scene at the wrong structural moment dies, a gripping story in a monotone dies, brilliant actors at meaningless distances die — the vocabulary tells you which part is failing.

activities.anchor: Change any rung of that ladder
activities.caption: rebuild the tragedy ladder
activities.name: dramaTragedyOrder

config.prompt: Antigone walks Aristotle's ladder exactly — put the rungs in order:
items: Inciting incident — the brothers kill each other; Creon forbids the burial of one
Rising action — Antigone defies him and buries her brother
The sentence — Creon orders her sealed in a cave
Recognition — the prophet Tiresias warns, and Creon sees his stubborn error
Reversal, too late — Antigone has killed herself, and his wife follows in grief
config.why: Recognition arrives after the action has built, and it is tragic because it comes too late to prevent the reversal — swap any two steps and the play's meaning moves.

activities.anchor: an examiner will expect you to notice
activities.caption: pair each archetype with its function
activities.name: dramaArchetypeMatch

config.prompt: Ready-made shapes of character — pair each with its function and example:

pairs.right: Hamlet — the central figure the play orbits
Fortinbras — acts decisively where Hamlet hesitates, and the comparison exposes both
Ophelia — draws out the protagonist's heart

config.why: Archetypes are starting points, not cages — the analytical move is noticing when a play uses one honestly and when it subverts it.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — playable dialogue
activities.name: dramaDialogueSpot

config.prompt: One of these dialogue rules is backwards — click it:
lines: 'I'm fine' can be played as a threat, a plea, a dismissal or a lie — the actor chooses which.
Subtext is what the character wants but does not say; the words and the want pull apart.
People under pressure speak in careful full paragraphs, explaining themselves completely.
A two-second silence before 'No' doubles the line's weight.
Lines that sound like writing usually close the scene down instead of handing the obstacle on.
config.correction: The opposite: under pressure people interrupt, deflect and answer a different question — economy, not paragraphs.
config.why: Every line is an action, a playable verb; a paragraph of explanation gives the other actor nothing to play off.

activities.caption: words vs body — drag the divider
activities.name: dramaBodyCompare

config.prompt: The asymmetric relationship — drag between the two channels:

before.label: The spoken word
before.text: 'I'm delighted for you' — pleasant, safe, socially correct. On its own, it closes the moment.

after.label: The body
after.text: A clenched jaw, lowered eyes, no step forward — the audience reads two scenes at once, and both land.

config.why: When the channels contradict, the body wins — which is why posture, gesture, face and gait are trained, not improvised.

activities.anchor: Pacing errors are structural in effect
activities.caption: fill the blanks — line rhythm
activities.name: dramaPacingCloze

config.text: Short exchanges %%0%% a scene; full sentences let it %%1%%. A scene that starts at full intensity has %%2%% left to go — and a scene that never accelerates reads as rehearsal rather than performance.
config.hint: The lesson's own verbs: what short lines do, what long sentences do, and what an early peak leaves.

activities.caption: bet before the reveal — which staging holds the room?
activities.name: dramaTensionPredict

config.q: Same waiting moment, two stagings: in one, the actor paces, wrings their hands, and the score swells; in the other, they sit motionless — a clock visible, a door unopened. Which holds the room?
choices: The pacing, hand-wringing version — visible tension
The motionless one with the clock and the unopened door
config.why: Displayed anxiety releases pressure instead of building it: the audience is told what to feel. Tension is the audience leaning forward — built from mystery, suspense, irony and anticipation, played in stillness.

config.root: Your devised piece is a week from performance and previewed flat. Walk the closing discipline.

start.text: First pass: sound off. What are you checking?

choices.label: Structure and physicality
choices.feedback: With the sound gone, shape and body are all that is left — exactly what this pass isolates.

choices.label: Dialogue quality
choices.feedback: Dialogue is the eyes-shut pass — sound off hides the very thing you are listening for.

eyes.text: Second pass: eyes shut. What does it isolate?

choices.label: Dialogue, pacing, dynamics
choices.feedback: Voice and time only — the ear catches monotone and rhythm the eye misses.

choices.label: Set and costume
choices.feedback: Design frames the piece, but eyes shut strips the visual frame — wrong pass.

want.text: Final discipline, at every moment of the run:

choices.label: Ask what the audience wants right now — and whether you are giving it or making them wait deliberately
choices.feedback: Deliberate waiting is tension; accidental waiting is a flat scene. That question is the whole integrated approach.

choices.label: Ask what you want right now
choices.feedback: Every element routes through the seats — the audience's attention is the currency, not the performer's.

wrongtool.text: Wrong pass for the job — sound off is the structure-and-physicality check. Run the passes in order.

design.text: Design frames the piece — lighting, sound, set, costume — but it is tuned last, after the passes that isolate the elements.

done.text: Sound off, eyes shut, then the audience question at every moment — rehearsal where the elements are tuned against attention.

selfish.text: The elements serve attention: cut what delays the goal, contrast what flattens, pace what rushes.

config.why: The integrated approach: structure schedules the tension, dialogue and physicality fill each moment, design frames it — and rehearsal tunes all of it against an audience.
